title: The menstrual cycle and its interaction with the oral microbiome and proinflammatory cytokines
summary:
This clinical study is investigating whether and how the menstrual cycle affects the composition of oral bacteria (the oral microbiome) and certain inflammatory molecules in saliva and blood. For this purpose, young, healthy women with regular menstrual cycles are examined by dentists several times during different phases of the cycle. Saliva, blood and tongue swab samples are taken and analyzed. 
The aim is to find out whether the natural hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle cause measurable changes in the immune system and oral microbiome. This could help to better understand (common) diseases such as periodontitis in the future and to better plan treatment times.
conditions: Only healthy test subjects are included.

interventions.name:
All treatments are standardized according to currently valid guidelines and follow the order below:
Periodontally healthy, young women (aged 18–35) with regular menstrual cycles are examined. There is no control group in the conventional sense.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- ASA status 1 and 2 
- Non-smoker
- Consent of the patient 
- Regular menstrual cycle
- Periodontal health (Chapple et al. 2018)
Exclusion criteria:
- Children (underage patients)
- Poor general condition (ASA status ≥3)
- no consent of the patient to participate in the study
- Diagnosed periodontitis disease
- Pregnancy, breastfeeding mothers
- Taking antibiotics
- Diabetes mellitus
- Rheumatoid arthritis
- Diseases with immunosuppression
- Patients with an increased risk of infective endocarditis
- Patients with an increased risk of drug-induced jaw necrosis
